attrs.management_says: The larger increase in accounts receivable ($90.8M incremental vs 2014) was primarily due to the timing of shipments.
attrs.numbers_show: Q4 2015 receivables jumped 55% year-over-year while Q4 revenue rose 30.8%; Q4 DSO rose from 28 to 34 days (E30). Full-year DSO rose from 33 to 40 days (E25), driven by the year-end snapshot. The incremental receivables increase (2015 Δ$153.8M vs 2014 Δ$65.1M ≈ $88.7M) aligns with the cited $90.8M.

attrs.management_says: In 2014, the receivables increase was attributed to a higher proportion of international sales with longer payment terms; in 2015, the incremental increase is attributed to shipment timing.
attrs.numbers_show: International revenue grew strongly in both years (2014: +$131.6M, 2015: +$185.4M per E45, E43). The 2015 explanation focuses on the incremental change, not the base effect. The quarterly DSO pattern (Q1-Q3 relatively stable, Q4 sharp rise) supports a 2015-specific timing effect, but the ongoing international mix may also contribute to the elevated DSO level.

attrs.management_says: Accounts receivable increased $90.8M more in 2015 than in 2014 primarily due to the timing of shipments.
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables grew 55% ($279.8M → $433.6M) vs. revenue 28.5%; DSO rose 33→40 days. Q4 receivables jumped 55% YoY ($279.8M → $433.6M) with DSO rising 28→34 days, consistent with late-quarter shipments. The incremental YoY increase in receivables change is ~$88.7M, close to the cited $90.8M.
